recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future document-stylesheet changes should wait for a later work-group decision that changes the stylesheet resolution or document rendering model.
issue_request: FHIR-8027 was a Published FHIR-core DSTU1 clarification request. It reported that the old statement recommending internal stylesheet references when a document was not safe to view without the stylesheet appeared to contradict the adjacent rule that stylesheets SHALL NOT change clinical meaning, and it asked whether a common stylesheet was supplied. The Persuasive with Modification resolution required replacing that unsafe-to-view rationale with a technical/policy explanation for preferring internal stylesheet references.
initial_application: Git-svn commit b39b208cfd750898e66e5b1a68cad49f5be5b2a7, '#8027 - adjust language about stylesheets', changed source/documents.html and records SVN revision 5824, matching the Jira application comment. Later QA commits 810b01be59f943f06331caf0b09629bb60c8497d and fe148b2af9615e85a33c70d0633fe7f6a57d4b9b normalized encoding, whitespace, and grammar without changing the substance.
additional_context: source/documents.html is in current build scope through source/hierarchy.xml. The current page uses the applied broader phrase 'external content' rather than the Jira resolution's narrower 'HTTP content', and this preserves the approved rationale while avoiding a less accurate protocol-specific limitation. Related document-presentation work, including FHIR-5248 and FHIR-7388, addressed adjacent clinical-meaning and presentation-change wording.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source says relative internal references SHOULD be used for stylesheets because the viewer may be unable to resolve external content at viewing time due to technical problems or local policy decisions, and it retains the adjacent SHALL NOT rule preventing stylesheets from changing clinical meaning.

related_jiras.note: Earlier adjacent document-presentation clarification added the stylesheet clinical-meaning guardrail that FHIR-8027 references; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Related Published document-page issue softened presentation-change language around the same clinical-meaning concern.
